question: Should OpenClaw adopt `gateway.suspend.prepare`, `gateway.suspend.status`, and `gateway.suspend.resume` with a fixed two-minute renewable lease as the supported host-snapshot contract, while third-party transports and arbitrary plugin work remain outside its guarantee?
rationale: Code review can assess the mechanism, but only maintainers can commit the project to this durable operator API, timing policy, and limitation boundary.

options.title: Adopt the bounded contract
options.body: Accept the core RPC and lease contract after exact-head live proof is supplied and preserve the documented exclusions.

options.title: Expose activity signals first
options.body: Defer the mutating fence and add only owner-approved read-only busy-state primitives until lifecycle semantics are settled.

options.title: Decline core suspension
options.body: Keep host lifecycle coordination outside core and rely on existing health, restart, and plugin surfaces.

recommendation.title: Adopt the bounded contract
recommendation.body: Accept the core RPC and lease contract after exact-head live proof is supplied and preserve the documented exclusions.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the central restart and drain history, is the current assignee, and has the strongest direct history across the affected Gateway and protocol surfaces.
